messages:
matt: quick sync — we need a proposal for the microbatch / queueing dashboard before next week's ops review. main ask: batch size distribution, queue wait percentiles, and a saturation indicator that ties runtime queues to infra limits.

sana: +1. runtime can emit per-worker histograms for batch_size and a summary for enqueue_wait_seconds. unsure about cardinality if we include model/version tags.

lee: infra can add per-node GPU queue_depth and gpu_util_pct gauges. we should avoid high-cardinality labels (region, rack, instance-type ok).

olga: product wants a single console view that shows: current fill-rate, 95/99 wait time, and an action hint (e.g., scale policy link or fallback model). keep it concise for SRE oncall.

matt: rough metric names proposal: `redwood_runtime_batch_size_hist` (histogram), `redwood_runtime_enqueue_wait_seconds` (summary), `redwood_node_gpu_queue_depth` (gauge), `redwood_node_gpu_utilization_percent` (gauge). thoughts?

sana: those look fine. can we include a `batch_fill_rate` gauge derived in the metrics pipeline? i.e., fraction of batches with size >= target_window_size.

tj: for alerts, propose:
- queue_wait_p95 > 250ms for 5m -> page
- queue_wait_p99 > 1s for 2m -> page
- avg_gpu_util > 95% & queue_depth > X -> page
We need a playbook for incident steps (fallback to smaller model, divert to hosted pool).

lee: regarding ingestion: runtime emits per-worker hist buckets, but our metrics pipeline should aggregate to rollup granularity by `model_family` + `deployment_tier` to keep storage sane. we can run an hourly downsample.

matt: mock PromQLs for dashboard panels:```promql
# p95 enqueue wait by model
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_runtime_enqueue_wait_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model_family))
# avg batch size
sum(rate(redwood_runtime_batch_size_sum[5m])) by (model_family) / sum(rate(redwood_runtime_batch_size_count[5m])) by (model_family)
```

sana: nice. also add a heatmap for batch size distribution (per-model_family) and a line for node saturation overlay.

olga: UX: main console tile = single-row summary (fill-rate | p95 wait | saturation icon). clicking expands to panels: distribution heatmap, wait-time percentiles, per-region saturation. also show recommended action (scale up / switch routing policy).

tj: we should surface routing policy impacts — i.e., when cheap-routing is on, batch sizes drop and wait times improve but cost increases. maybe a small sparkline showing routing policy version tag.

matt: action items I can take: 1) draft dashboard JSON prototype with panels and variables, 2) land runtime metric changes (sana), 3) infra gauges + low-cardinality label plan (lee), 4) alert thresholds + playbook (tj & olga). I'll post the prototype by EOD Friday.

sana: I'll open a runtime PR to expose `redwood_runtime_enqueue_wait_seconds_bucket` and `redwood_runtime_batch_size_{sum,count}` with `model_family` and `deployment_tier` labels.

lee: I'll add node gauges and a sample ingestion transform to aggregate by model_family. expect a doc + PR for metrics pipeline.

tj: I'll draft alert rules and the short runbook steps. can pair with olga for the UX phrasing.

matt: thanks — if anyone has objections to the metric names/labels speak now. otherwise I'll draft the dashboard and share link. :thumbsup:

dashbot: deploy status: no deploys in progress.

olga: no objections from product. one ask: include a small note in the expanded panel about interpretability of p99 for very low qps deploys.

matt: good call — will add a tooltip: "p99 unreliable under < 1r/s; consider synthetic load evals".

sana: ack, will include a test exporter that can generate synthetic traces for low-qps models so dashboards show meaningful percentiles.

lee: ok, I'll coordinate retention and downsample windows with infra monitoring.

matt: perfect. wrapping up — next check-in Tue morning after prototype. cheers.
